canonical_statement: EMPEROR-Preserved evaluated whether empagliflozin reduces major heart-failure outcomes in patients with chronic heart failure and a left ventricular ejection fraction above 40%.
EMPEROR-Preserved was a randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled, event-driven phase III trial.
The trial was conducted at 622 centers in 23 countries.
Ethics committees at each center approved the trial and all participants provided written informed consent.
An independent data monitoring committee reviewed safety data and the prespecified interim analysis according to stopping boundaries.
A clinical events committee adjudicated outcomes in a blinded manner using prespecified definitions.
An independent statistician replicated and verified the trial analyses.
Academic executive-committee members provided an independent interpretation of the results and the authors decided to submit the manuscript.
The trial was funded by Boehringer Ingelheim and Eli Lilly.
Boehringer Ingelheim was responsible for data collection and storage.
The article states that author disclosure forms are available with the full text.
The article states that an author-provided data sharing statement is available with the full text.
Participants were adults aged at least 18 years at screening (at least 20 years in Japan).

inclusion_criteria: Age ≥18 years at screening; Japan ≥20 years.

canonical_statement: Eligible participants had chronic heart failure diagnosed for at least 3 months and current NYHA functional class II through IV.

canonical_statement: Body-mass index had to be below 45 kg/m² at screening.
Patients with acute decompensated heart failure requiring intravenous diuretics, vasodilators, inotropes, or mechanical support within 1 week of screening or during screening were excluded.

exclusion_criteria: Recent acute decompensated HF requiring IV/mechanical support.

canonical_statement: Symptomatic hypotension or systolic blood pressure below 100 mm Hg at screening or randomization was an exclusion criterion.

exclusion_criteria: Symptomatic hypotension or SBP <100 mm Hg.

canonical_statement: Impaired renal function with eGFR below 20 mL/min/1.73 m² or dialysis at screening was an exclusion criterion.
Current or recent SGLT2 or combined SGLT1/2 inhibitor use within 12 weeks was excluded, and discontinuation solely to enroll was not permitted.
A history of ketoacidosis was an exclusion criterion.
Participants assigned to the intervention received empagliflozin 10 mg once daily in addition to usual therapy.
Participants assigned to the control group received matching placebo once daily in addition to usual therapy.
After a 4-to-28-day screening period, eligible patients were randomized 1:1 in double-blind fashion.
Randomization used permuted blocks and was stratified by geographic region, diabetes status, eGFR below versus at least 60 mL/min/1.73 m², and LVEF below versus at least 50%.
After randomization, clinicians could initiate or alter appropriate treatments for heart failure or other conditions at their discretion.
Participants were to be followed for prespecified outcomes throughout the trial whether or not they continued study medication or protocol procedures.
The primary outcome was time to first adjudicated cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure.

canonical_statement: The first key secondary outcome was total adjudicated hospitalizations for heart failure, including first and recurrent events.

concept.text: Total first and recurrent hospitalizations for heart failure

canonical_statement: The second key secondary outcome was the annual rate of decline in eGFR during double-blind treatment.

concept.text: Annual eGFR slope during double-blind treatment

canonical_statement: The primary outcome and two key secondary outcomes were tested in a prespecified hierarchical sequence to preserve the overall type I error rate.

The primary time-to-event analysis used a Cox proportional-hazards model adjusted for age, sex, geographic region, diabetes status, LVEF, and eGFR, with alpha 0.0497 after accounting for one interim analysis.
Total first and recurrent heart-failure hospitalizations were analyzed with a joint frailty model treating cardiovascular death as informative censoring, at alpha 0.0497.
The eGFR slope outcome used on-treatment data in a random-coefficient model and was assigned alpha 0.001.
Treatment effects outside the hierarchical testing procedure were not adjusted for multiple comparisons and their intervals were not intended for definitive treatment-effect inference.
No imputation was used for missing data.
The event-driven design targeted 841 adjudicated primary events for 90% power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.80.

Enrollment was increased from an initial plan of 4126 to at least 5750 because blinded event-rate monitoring indicated slower event accumulation; the target event count was unchanged and no unblinded trial data were used for the increase.
A prespecified interim efficacy analysis occurred after approximately 500 primary events; the data monitoring committee did not recommend early termination.
A total of 11,583 patients were screened and 5,988 were randomized.
Randomization assigned 2,997 participants to empagliflozin and 2,991 to placebo.
Baseline mean age was 71.8 years with empagliflozin and 71.9 years with placebo.
Women comprised 44.6% of the empagliflozin group and 44.7% of the placebo group.
Mean LVEF was 54.3% in both treatment groups; approximately one third of each group had LVEF 40 to <50%, one third 50 to <60%, and one third at least 60%.
Diabetes was present in 48.9% of empagliflozin participants and 49.2% of placebo participants.
Mean eGFR was 60.6 mL/min/1.73 m² in both groups and about half of participants had eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m².
At baseline, approximately 81% received a renin-angiotensin-system inhibitor, 37% a mineralocorticoid-receptor antagonist, and 86% a beta-blocker.
Median follow-up for the primary outcome was 26.2 months (IQR 18.1 to 33.1).
Trial medication was stopped for reasons other than death by 696 empagliflozin participants (23.2%) and 699 placebo participants (23.4%).
Vital status was unknown at trial end for 17 participants (0.6%) in the empagliflozin group and 19 (0.6%) in the placebo group.
The primary composite occurred in 415 of 2,997 participants (13.8%) with empagliflozin and 511 of 2,991 (17.1%) with placebo; HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.69 to 0.90; p<0.001).

Safety analyses were based on participants who received at least one dose of randomized trial medication.
The supplied final clinical trial protocol is version 4.0, dated 20 Nov 2019, based on Global Amendment 03.
The supplied revised Trial Statistical Analysis Plan is dated 12 Feb 2021 and incorporates Revised Protocol 03.

The TSAP history records a 23 Jan 2020 revision that excluded the follow-up period from intention-to-treat efficacy analyses while adding sensitivity analyses including all events for the primary endpoint and recurrent heart-failure hospitalization.
The TSAP revision added a baseline-by-time interaction to the renal-slope model.
The protocol defined the trial as phase III and specified once-daily empagliflozin 10 mg versus placebo in chronic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
The authors concluded that empagliflozin reduced the combined risk of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure in patients with heart failure and preserved ejection fraction.

The authors attributed the primary-composite benefit mainly to fewer hospitalizations for heart failure and stated that empagliflozin did not appear to affect cardiovascular or all-cause mortality in this trial.
The authors stated that the benefit was seen with or without diabetes and across prespecified ejection-fraction subgroups.

Approximately 23% of participants discontinued study medication for reasons other than death; the authors noted that this high discontinuation rate might have attenuated the observed treatment effect toward the null.
The trial did not demonstrate a cardiovascular-mortality effect with a confidence interval excluding no effect: HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.76 to 1.09).
Results outside the prespecified testing hierarchy were not multiplicity-adjusted and were explicitly not intended for definitive treatment-effect inference.
